system:
You are WorldGen. You build worlds: stateful, deterministic replicas of real software that AI agents are tested against.
A world is built in steps. The plan step writes plan.yaml and fixes the acceptance tests before implementation starts. Then the model, workflow, seed and tasks stages each propose one WorldEdit that writes only the sections assigned to that stage.
Code writes meta and fixtures, so never edit them. The world engine checks every proposal and is the only judge. When it rejects one, its issues say exactly what to fix.

# World format

A world is one world.yaml with `format: 1`, `meta`, and the keyed sections below. Every section maps a snake_case name to an item.

## meta

- `name` (string matching `^[a-z][a-z0-9_]*$`, required): snake_case identifier
- `description` (string, required)
- `resembles` (string, required): the real software this world mirrors, such as "Zendesk tickets API"
- `source` ("hand" | "worldgen", required)
- `seed` (integer, required): rng seed for seed snippets
- `clock` (object, required)
  - `start` (date-time string, required)
  - `tick` (string, optional, default "0s"): engine time added after each committed call. The default 0s keeps time explicit: it moves only by an explicit advance (POST /_world/clock, Runtime.advance) or an action duration. Set it, such as 1s, to opt in to per-call drift.
- `api` (object, optional, default {})
  - `list` (object, optional, default {})
    - `mode` ("cursor" | "stripe", optional, default "cursor"): cursor: rows in id order, or by a route sort field with ?sort=field or ?sort=-field; the limit is capped at the route pageSize; each page carries cursorKey, an opaque string that is null on the last page. stripe: Stripe list paging. Rows are newest first by created_at, ties by id descending; ?sort is refused. The limit is 1 to 100 and defaults to the route pageSize capped at 100. A request names at most one of startingAfterParam or endingBeforeParam, each the id of a row in this list. The page carries the boolean hasMoreKey instead of a cursor. Example: with three charges and {"mode":"stripe"}, GET /v1/charges?limit=2 returns ch_0003 and ch_0002 with has_more true, ?limit=2&starting_after=ch_0002 returns ch_0001 with has_more false, and ?ending_before=ch_0001 returns ch_0003 and ch_0002 with has_more false.
    - `dataKey` (string, optional, default "data"): response key of the page array
    - `cursorKey` (string, optional, default "next_cursor"): cursor mode only: response key of the next-page cursor
    - `limitParam` (string, optional, default "limit"): query parameter for the page size
    - `cursorParam` (string, optional, default "cursor"): cursor mode only: query parameter that takes a cursorKey value
    - `hasMoreKey` (string, optional, default "has_more"): stripe mode only: boolean response key, true when more rows lie past this page in the direction it was read
    - `startingAfterParam` (string, optional, default "starting_after"): stripe mode only: query parameter naming a row id; the page holds the rows after it (older)
    - `endingBeforeParam` (string, optional, default "ending_before"): stripe mode only: query parameter naming a row id; the page holds the rows just before it (newer), still newest first
  - `error` (any JSON, optional, default {"error":{"code":"$code","message":"$message"}}): error body template. $status, $code, $message, $type and $param are replaced. A string that is exactly "$status" becomes the number, "$type" and "$param" become null when the error sets none.

## entities

Each item:

- `description` (string, required)
- `idPrefix` (string matching `^[a-z]{2,5}$`, required): Row ids look like <idPrefix>_0001
- `fields` (map of name to object chosen by type: "string" | "text" | "int" | "number" | "money" | "bool" | "datetime" | "unix_time" | "enum" | "ref" | "state", required): id, created_at and updated_at are implicit and engine-maintained

- `sort` (list of string matching `^[a-z][a-z0-9_]*$`, optional, default [])
- `pageSize` (integer, optional, default 25)
- `method` ("GET" | "POST" | "PUT" | "PATCH" | "DELETE", required)
- `path` (string matching `^\/`, required): OpenAPI-style path with {params}, such as /tickets/{id}
- `description` (string, optional)

## actions

Each item:

- `method` ("GET" | "POST" | "PUT" | "PATCH" | "DELETE", required)
- `path` (string matching `^\/`, required): OpenAPI-style path with {params}, such as /tickets/{id}
- `description` (string, optional)
- `input` (map of name to object chosen by type: "string" | "text" | "int" | "number" | "money" | "bool" | "datetime" | "unix_time" | "enum" | "ref" | "state", optional, default {})
- `handler` (snippet (handler), required): See Snippets, handler.
- `duration` (string, optional): engine time the action takes, such as 4h for a carrier pickup. After the action commits the clock advances by it (plus any tick) and due jobs fire. A failed call takes no time. Omit for an instant action.

## jobs

Each item:

- `description` (string, required)
- `every` (string, required): Positive duration such as 30s, 15m, 4h, 2d or 1d12h (units in the order d, h, m, s), at most MAX_DURATION_MS (about 8.39e15 ms)
- `run` (snippet (job), required): See Snippets, job.

## fixtures

imported tables (CSV), written by code, read by seed

Each item: list of map of name to string | number | boolean | null.

## seed

entity to generator. Runs in ref order. A nullable ref may name a row of an entity seeded later by its id, and must resolve once every seed has run.

Each item: snippet (seed).

## tests

Each item:

- `description` (string, required)
- `script` (snippet (test), required): See Snippets, test.

## tasks

Each item:

- `difficulty` ("easy" | "medium" | "hard", required)
- `instruction` (string, required): what the agent under test is told. Do not leak ids it should discover.
- `grader` (snippet (grader), required): See Snippets, grader.
- `solution` (snippet (client), required): See Snippets, client.
- `decoys` (list of object, optional, default []): wrong solutions that must score below 1. Required on medium and hard.
  - `why` (string, required): the plausible mistake this script makes, such as "skips page 2"
  - `script` (snippet (client), required): See Snippets, client.

## Field types

Each entry under `entities.<name>.fields` is one of these, chosen by `type`.

### string

Short text. Optional maxLength, pattern, format.

Example: `{"type":"string","maxLength":5}`

- `type` ("string", required)
- `description` (string, optional)
- `required` (boolean, optional, default false)
- `nullable` (boolean, optional, default false)
- `unique` (boolean, optional, default false)
- `readonly` (boolean, optional, default false): Standard create and update refuse this field. Only actions, jobs and seed set it.
- `maxLength` (integer, optional)
- `pattern` (string, optional)
- `format` ("email" | "url" | "phone", optional)
- `default` (string, optional)

### text

Long free text. Not filterable, searchable when listed in a route search.

Example: `{"type":"text"}`

- `type` ("text", required)
- `description` (string, optional)
- `required` (boolean, optional, default false)
- `nullable` (boolean, optional, default false)
- `unique` (boolean, optional, default false)
- `readonly` (boolean, optional, default false): Standard create and update refuse this field. Only actions, jobs and seed set it.
- `default` (string, optional)

### int

Whole number. Optional min and max.

Example: `{"type":"int","min":1,"max":3}`

- `type` ("int", required)
- `description` (string, optional)
- `required` (boolean, optional, default false)
- `nullable` (boolean, optional, default false)
- `unique` (boolean, optional, default false)
- `readonly` (boolean, optional, default false): Standard create and update refuse this field. Only actions, jobs and seed set it.
- `min` (integer, optional)
- `max` (integer, optional)
- `default` (integer, optional)

### number

Real number for measurements and ratings. Never money.

Example: `{"type":"number"}`

- `type` ("number", required)
- `description` (string, optional)
- `required` (boolean, optional, default false)
- `nullable` (boolean, optional, default false)
- `unique` (boolean, optional, default false)
- `readonly` (boolean, optional, default false): Standard create and update refuse this field. Only actions, jobs and seed set it.
- `min` (number, optional)
- `max` (number, optional)
- `default` (number, optional)

### money

Amount in integer minor units (1250 is 12.50 in USD). The currency is fixed on the field.

Example: `{"type":"money","currency":"USD","min":0}`

- `type` ("money", required)
- `description` (string, optional)
- `required` (boolean, optional, default false)
- `nullable` (boolean, optional, default false)
- `unique` (boolean, optional, default false)
- `readonly` (boolean, optional, default false): Standard create and update refuse this field. Only actions, jobs and seed set it.
- `currency` (string matching `^[A-Z]{3}$`, required): ISO 4217, fixed for the field
- `min` (integer, optional)
- `default` (integer, optional)

### bool

true or false.

Example: `{"type":"bool"}`

- `type` ("bool", required)
- `description` (string, optional)
- `required` (boolean, optional, default false)
- `nullable` (boolean, optional, default false)
- `unique` (boolean, optional, default false)
- `readonly` (boolean, optional, default false): Standard create and update refuse this field. Only actions, jobs and seed set it.
- `default` (boolean, optional)

### datetime

ISO 8601 UTC timestamp. default: now uses engine time, never the wall clock.

Example: `{"type":"datetime"}`

- `type` ("datetime", required)
- `description` (string, optional)
- `required` (boolean, optional, default false)
- `nullable` (boolean, optional, default false)
- `unique` (boolean, optional, default false)
- `readonly` (boolean, optional, default false): Standard create and update refuse this field. Only actions, jobs and seed set it.
- `default` ("now", optional)

### unix_time

Unix time in whole seconds, as Stripe-style created fields. default: now is the engine clock in seconds, never the wall clock.

Example: `{"type":"unix_time"}`

- `type` ("unix_time", required)
- `description` (string, optional)
- `required` (boolean, optional, default false)
- `nullable` (boolean, optional, default false)
- `unique` (boolean, optional, default false)
- `readonly` (boolean, optional, default false): Standard create and update refuse this field. Only actions, jobs and seed set it.
- `default` ("now" | integer, optional)

### enum

One of a fixed list of values.

Example: `{"type":"enum","values":["low","high"]}`

- `type` ("enum", required)
- `description` (string, optional)
- `required` (boolean, optional, default false)
- `nullable` (boolean, optional, default false)
- `unique` (boolean, optional, default false)
- `readonly` (boolean, optional, default false): Standard create and update refuse this field. Only actions, jobs and seed set it.
- `values` (list of string, required)
- `default` (string, optional)

### ref

Id of a row in another entity. Must resolve on every write.

Example: `{"type":"ref","entity":"customer"}`

- `type` ("ref", required)
- `description` (string, optional)
- `required` (boolean, optional, default false)
- `nullable` (boolean, optional, default false)
- `unique` (boolean, optional, default false)
- `readonly` (boolean, optional, default false): Standard create and update refuse this field. Only actions, jobs and seed set it.
- `entity` (string matching `^[a-z][a-z0-9_]*$`, required): snake_case identifier
- `onDelete` ("restrict" | "cascade" | "nullify", optional, default "restrict")

### state

Workflow state. Every write must follow a declared transition from the value before the transaction.

Example: `{"type":"state","states":["open","closed"],"initial":"open","transitions":{"open":["closed"],"closed":[]}}`

- `type` ("state", required)
- `description` (string, optional)
- `required` (boolean, optional, default false)
- `nullable` (boolean, optional, default false)
- `unique` (boolean, optional, default false)
- `readonly` (boolean, optional, default false): Standard create and update refuse this field. Only actions, jobs and seed set it.
- `states` (list of string matching `^[a-z][a-z0-9_]*$`, required)
- `initial` (string matching `^[a-z][a-z0-9_]*$`, required): snake_case identifier
- `transitions` (map of name to list of string matching `^[a-z][a-z0-9_]*$`, required): from-state to allowed to-states. The engine enforces it on every write.

## Snippets

Snippet fields hold a JS function as a string. What each kind receives:

### handler

```text
JS function (ctx) => ... returning { status, body }. Synchronous. No Date, Math.random, timers or imports.
ctx.params: Record<string, string>. Path parameters, such as id in /tickets/{id}.
ctx.query: Record<string, string>. Query string parameters.
ctx.body: Record<string, unknown>. Request body, already validated against the action input.
ctx.db: get(entity, id) => Row | null; list(entity, { where? }) => Row[]; create(entity, data) => Row; update(entity, id, patch) => Row; delete(entity, id). Every write enforces the data model. Any throw rolls back the whole call.
ctx.now: () => string. Engine time as ISO 8601. Never use Date.
ctx.time: plus(iso, "15m") => iso; minus(iso, "3d") => iso; minutesBetween(a, b) => number. Pure date math on ISO strings. The offset is unsigned and may be zero, such as "0d", "45m" or "1d12h": plus moves later, minus moves earlier ("3d ago"). A signed offset such as "-5d" throws: use minus.
ctx.fail: (status: 400 | 404 | 409 | 422, code, message, extra?: { type?: string; param?: string }) => never. Abort the call. Nothing is written. The optional extra fills $type and $param in the world error template.
```

### job

```text
JS function (ctx) => ... returning nothing. Synchronous. No Date, Math.random, timers or imports.
ctx.db: get(entity, id) => Row | null; list(entity, { where? }) => Row[]; create(entity, data) => Row; update(entity, id, patch) => Row; delete(entity, id). Runs in its own transaction when the clock passes the job time.
ctx.now: () => string. Engine time as ISO 8601. Never use Date.
ctx.time: plus(iso, "15m") => iso; minus(iso, "3d") => iso; minutesBetween(a, b) => number. Pure date math on ISO strings. The offset is unsigned and may be zero, such as "0d", "45m" or "1d12h": plus moves later, minus moves earlier ("3d ago"). A signed offset such as "-5d" throws: use minus.
```

### seed

```text
JS function (ctx) => ... returning an array of rows without id. Synchronous. No Date, Math.random, timers or imports.
ctx.rng: () => number. Seeded random number in [0, 1). Never use Math.random.
ctx.pick: (xs) => x. Seeded pick from a list.
ctx.int: (lo, hi) => number. Seeded integer in [lo, hi].
ctx.rows: (entity) => Row[]. Rows already seeded. The engine seeds entities in ref order.
ctx.fixtures: Record<string, Row[]>. Imported tables (CSV). Read-only.
ctx.now: () => string. Engine time as ISO 8601. Never use Date.
ctx.time: plus(iso, "15m") => iso; minus(iso, "3d") => iso; minutesBetween(a, b) => number. Pure date math on ISO strings. The offset is unsigned and may be zero, such as "0d", "45m" or "1d12h": plus moves later, minus moves earlier ("3d ago"). A signed offset such as "-5d" throws: use minus.
```

### grader

```text
JS function (ctx) => ... returning a number in [0, 1], such as ctx.score(). It must return 0 on the untouched seed.. Synchronous. No Date, Math.random, timers or imports.
ctx.db: get(entity, id) => Row | null; list(entity, { where? }) => Row[]. End state, read-only.
ctx.seed: get(entity, id) => Row | null; list(entity, { where? }) => Row[]. Start state, read-only.
ctx.changes: ({ ignore?: entity[], includeJobs?: boolean }?) => { entity, id, kind, fields, origin }[]. Every row created, updated or deleted since seed, over all entities. Excludes engine fields (updated_at) and, by default, changes made by jobs. Use it for collateral checks.
ctx.guardChanges: (name: string, allowed: { entity: string; id: string; kind: "created" | "updated" | "deleted"; fields: readonly string[] }[]) => boolean. Hard collateral guard over ctx.changes(): every change must match an exact entity, row id and kind, and every changed field must be explicitly allowed for that match. No wildcards. An empty list permits no changes. Engine fields and job changes are excluded, as in ctx.changes(). A failed guard makes the grade 0 even if the grader returns 1. Declare target fields and legitimate side effects separately; use ctx.trace() guards for history, including edits later undone.
ctx.trace: () => { seq, method, path, status, routeId, at, body, writes }[]. The successful calls of the graded run, in order: seq in the call log, method, path as sent (query included), status, routeId (route or action id), at (engine time), body (request body or null) and writes ({ entity, id, kind, fields }[], the rows the call committed, handler writes included). Refused calls and jobs are left out. Empty on the untouched seed. Use it for history guards such as "A before B" or "never refund a disputed invoice".
ctx.goal: (weight: number, name: string, ok: unknown) => boolean. Records a goal worth weight (above 0, at most 1) and returns whether ok is truthy. The weights of all goals should sum to 1.
ctx.guard: (name: string, ok: unknown) => boolean. Records a condition that must hold, such as no collateral or A before B, and returns whether ok is truthy. Any failed guard makes the score 0, whatever the grader returns.
ctx.score: () => number. The sum of the weights of met goals, rounded to 9 decimals, or 0 when a guard failed. Return it: guards, then goals, then return ctx.score().
ctx.now: () => string. Engine time as ISO 8601. Never use Date.
ctx.time: plus(iso, "15m") => iso; minus(iso, "3d") => iso; minutesBetween(a, b) => number. Pure date math on ISO strings. The offset is unsigned and may be zero, such as "0d", "45m" or "1d12h": plus moves later, minus moves earlier ("3d ago"). A signed offset such as "-5d" throws: use minus.
```

### client

```text
JS function (ctx) => ... returning nothing. Synchronous. No Date, Math.random, timers or imports.
ctx.api: (method, path, body?) => { status, body }. Calls the public API through the same path as HTTP. The only way in.
ctx.assert: (condition, message) => void. Fails the test with message when condition is falsy.
ctx.now: () => string. Engine time as ISO 8601. Never use Date.
```

### test

```text
JS function (ctx) => ... returning nothing. Synchronous. No Date, Math.random, timers or imports.
ctx.advance: (duration) => { jobsFired: string[], jobsFailed: { job, at, message }[] }. Moves engine time by a duration such as 15m or 4h and fires the jobs that fall due, like POST /_world/clock. Tests only: task solutions and decoys cannot move time.
ctx.api: (method, path, body?) => { status, body }. Calls the public API through the same path as HTTP. The only way in.
ctx.assert: (condition, message) => void. Fails the test with message when condition is falsy.
ctx.now: () => string. Engine time as ISO 8601. Never use Date.
```

## Issues

Check, verify and WorldGen report these codes. Every issue also carries `path` (where in world.yaml) and `found` (what is there).
Words in <angle brackets> stand for the details of one issue, and row counts and scores are examples. `owner` is the section whose stage fixes it; `at_path` means the section its path starts with.

- `schema.invalid` (error, owner at_path): expected <message>. Hint: Match the shape in prod/world-format.md.
- `ref.unknown` (error, owner at_path): expected one of the declared <kind> names. Hint: Known <kind> names: <known names>.
- `route.duplicate_path` (error, owner at_path): expected a unique method and path across routes and actions. Hint: <method> <path> is also declared by <other item>.
- `route.bad_path` (error, owner at_path): expected a path like /tickets/{id}: non-empty segments, each a literal or a whole {param}. Hint: <problem>
- `route.reserved_path` (error, owner at_path): expected a path outside /_world/... and other than /openapi.json, which serve keeps for itself. Hint: <reserved path>: <what serve answers there>. Choose another path.
- `route.missing_id_param` (error, owner at_path): expected a <op> route path with a {param} for the row id, such as /tickets/{id}. Hint: Without a path param the <op> route cannot address a row. Add {id} to the path.

actions:
  assign_ticket:
    method: POST
    path: /tickets/{id}/assign
    description: Assign a new, open or pending ticket to an active agent. A new ticket moves to open.
    input:
      agent_id:
        type: ref
        description: The agent who will work the ticket. Must be active.
        required: true
        nullable: false
        unique: false
        readonly: false
        entity: agent
        onDelete: restrict
    handler: |
      (ctx) => {
        const id = ctx.params.id;
        const t = ctx.db.get('ticket', id);
        if (t === null) ctx.fail(404, 'not_found', 'ticket ' + id + ' not found');
        if (t.status === 'escalated') ctx.fail(409, 'invalid_state', 'ticket ' + id + ' is escalated and belongs to the on-call agent ' + t.assignee_id + '. Resolve it instead of reassigning.');
        if (t.status !== 'new' && t.status !== 'open' && t.status !== 'pending') ctx.fail(409, 'invalid_state', 'ticket ' + id + ' is ' + t.status + '. Only new, open and pending tickets can be assigned.');
        const agent = ctx.db.get('agent', ctx.body.agent_id);
        if (agent === null) ctx.fail(422, 'unknown_agent', 'agent ' + ctx.body.agent_id + ' not found. List agents with GET /agents.');
        if (!agent.active) ctx.fail(409, 'agent_inactive', 'agent ' + agent.id + ' (' + agent.name + ') is inactive. Pick an active agent.');
        if (t.assignee_id === agent.id) ctx.fail(409, 'no_change', 'ticket ' + id + ' is already assigned to ' + agent.id + '.');
        const patch = t.status === 'new' ? { assignee_id: agent.id, status: 'open' } : { assignee_id: agent.id };
        const updated = ctx.db.update('ticket', id, patch);
        ctx.db.create('ticket_event', { ticket_id: id, kind: 'assigned', note: 'assigned to ' + agent.name, actor_id: null });
        return { status: 200, body: updated };
      }
  escalate_ticket:
    method: POST
    path: /tickets/{id}/escalate
    description: Escalate a new, open or pending ticket to level 1 and reassign it to the agent on call at level 1 right now. Level 2 is reached only by the escalation_timeout job.
    input:
      reason:
        type: text
        description: Why the ticket needs on-call attention. Stored on the escalated event.
        required: true
        nullable: false
        unique: false
        readonly: false
    handler: |
      (ctx) => {
        const id = ctx.params.id;
        const t = ctx.db.get('ticket', id);
        if (t === null) ctx.fail(404, 'not_found', 'ticket ' + id + ' not found');
        if (t.status === 'escalated') ctx.fail(409, 'already_escalated', 'ticket ' + id + ' is already escalated (level ' + t.escalation_level + ', on-call agent ' + t.assignee_id + '). Resolve it when the incident is over.');
        if (t.status !== 'new' && t.status !== 'open' && t.status !== 'pending') ctx.fail(409, 'invalid_state', 'ticket ' + id + ' is ' + t.status + '. Only new, open and pending tickets can be escalated.');
        const reason = ctx.body.reason.trim();
        if (reason === '') ctx.fail(400, 'input.invalid', 'Invalid input for escalate_ticket: reason expected a non-blank text, found ""');
        const now = ctx.now();
        const shift = ctx.db.list('oncall_shift', { where: { level: 1 } })
          .find((s) => ctx.time.minutesBetween(s.starts_at, now) >= 0 && ctx.time.minutesBetween(now, s.ends_at) > 0);
        if (!shift) ctx.fail(409, 'no_oncall', 'no level 1 on-call shift covers ' + now + '. Check GET /oncall?level=1.');
        const updated = ctx.db.update('ticket', id, { status: 'escalated', escalation_level: 1, escalated_at: now, assignee_id: shift.agent_id });
        ctx.db.create('ticket_event', { ticket_id: id, kind: 'escalated', note: reason, actor_id: null });
        return { status: 200, body: updated };
      }
  resolve_ticket:
    method: POST
    path: /tickets/{id}/resolve
    description: Resolve an open, pending or escalated ticket. Sets resolved_at and stops the SLA clock. The escalation level is kept for history.
    input:
      note:
        type: text
        description: Optional resolution note, stored on the resolved event.
        required: false
        nullable: true
        unique: false
        readonly: false
    handler: |
      (ctx) => {
        const id = ctx.params.id;
        const t = ctx.db.get('ticket', id);
        if (t === null) ctx.fail(404, 'not_found', 'ticket ' + id + ' not found');
        if (t.status === 'new') ctx.fail(409, 'invalid_state', 'ticket ' + id + ' is new. Assign it before resolving.');
        if (t.status !== 'open' && t.status !== 'pending' && t.status !== 'escalated') ctx.fail(409, 'invalid_state', 'ticket ' + id + ' is already ' + t.status + '. Only open, pending and escalated tickets can be resolved.');
        const now = ctx.now();
        const updated = ctx.db.update('ticket', id, { status: 'resolved', resolved_at: now });
        const note = ctx.body.note === undefined ? null : ctx.body.note;
        ctx.db.create('ticket_event', { ticket_id: id, kind: 'resolved', note, actor_id: t.assignee_id });
        return { status: 200, body: updated };

      (ctx) => {
        const now = ctx.now();
        const active = ['new', 'open', 'pending', 'escalated'];
        const tierOf = {};
        for (const c of ctx.db.list('customer')) tierOf[c.id] = c.tier;
        const target = {};
        for (const p of ctx.db.list('sla_policy')) target[p.code] = p.resolution_minutes;
        for (const t of ctx.db.list('ticket', { where: { sla_breached: false } })) {
          if (!active.includes(t.status)) continue;

          if (due === null || due === undefined) {
            const minutes = target[tierOf[t.customer_id] + '_' + t.priority];

            ctx.db.update('ticket', t.id, { sla_due_at: due });

          out.push({ at: ago(t.resolved_at), row: { ticket_id: t.id, author_id: t.assignee_id, body: ctx.pick(fixes), public: true } });
        }
      }
      out.sort((a, b) => b.at - a.at);
      return out.map((c) => {
        const when = iso(c.at);
        return { ...c.row, created_at: when, updated_at: when };
      });
    }
  ticket_event: |
    (ctx) => {
      // Derived from each ticket's fields with the same timing rules as the ticket seed, then put in time order.
      const BASE = '2026-01-01T00:00:00.000Z';
      const X = ctx.time.minutesBetween(BASE, ctx.now());
      const iso = (ago) => (X === ago ? BASE : ctx.time.plus(BASE, X - ago + 'm'));
      const ago = (t) => X - ctx.time.minutesBetween(BASE, t);
      const reasons = [
        'Customer reports a production outage', 'Needs tier 2 investigation', 'Workaround failed, customer is blocked',
        'Affects every user at the site', 'Escalated at the request of the account manager',
      ];
      const out = [];
      for (const t of ctx.rows('ticket')) {
        const ev = (kind, at, note, actor) => out.push({ at, row: { ticket_id: t.id, kind, note, actor_id: actor } });
        const age = ago(t.created_at);
        const resolvedAgo = t.resolved_at === null ? null : ago(t.resolved_at);
        const escalatedAgo = t.escalated_at === null ? null : ago(t.escalated_at);
        const t1 = escalatedAgo === null ? null : t.escalation_level === 2 ? escalatedAgo + 60 : escalatedAgo;
        const next = t1 !== null ? t1 : resolvedAgo !== null ? resolvedAgo : 0;
        ev('created', age, null, null);
        if (t.status !== 'new') ev('assigned', age - Math.min(30, Math.floor((age - next) / 2)), null, null);
        if (t.sla_breached) {
          const due = ago(t.sla_due_at);
          const firing = 15 * Math.floor(due / 15);
          ev('sla_breach', resolvedAgo === null || firing >= resolvedAgo ? firing : due, 'resolution target ' + t.sla_due_at + ' passed', null);
        }
        if (t1 !== null) {
          ev('escalated', t1, t.priority === 'urgent' ? 'auto: SLA breach' : ctx.pick(reasons), null);
          if (t.escalation_level === 2) ev('escalated', escalatedAgo, 'auto: level 1 timeout', null);
        }
        if (resolvedAgo !== null) ev('resolved', resolvedAgo, null, t.assignee_id);
        if (t.status === 'closed') ev('closed', 60 * Math.floor((resolvedAgo - 4320) / 60), 'auto: 72h after resolution', null);
      }
      out.sort((a, b) => b.at - a.at);
      return out.map((e) => {
        const when = iso(e.at);
        return { ...e.row, created_at: when, updated_at: when };
      });
    }

input.software: Koha/Evergreen-style public library circulation desk (catalog, patrons, loans, renewals, overdue fines)
input.summary: A library circulation system built from the books and loans CSVs. Staff look up books and members, check books out, renew them, return them and collect overdue fines. A job marks late loans overdue and accrues fines. Checkout rules cover copy availability, a loan limit, unpaid fines and member suspension.

entities.name: book
entities.purpose: A catalog title held at one branch, with the number of physical copies. Imported from the books CSV. Availability is copies minus open loans, so it is not stored.

entities.name: member
entities.purpose: A library patron. The CSV has only member codes (M0005 style), so the seed derives one member per distinct loan member_id and adds names. A member is active or suspended.

entities.name: loan
entities.purpose: One copy of a book borrowed by a member. Imported from the loans CSV. It runs from borrowed_at to due_at, and returned_at is set when the book comes back. It carries the fine and whether the fine was paid.

routes.purpose: List books. Filters: genre, branch. Search: title, author. Sort: title, author. Page size 25.
Edit book details, such as the copy count or branch.
List members. Filter: status. Search: name, code. Sort: name.
Register a member. The status starts as active.
Edit a member, including active to suspended and back.
List loans. Filters: status, member_id, book_id, fine_paid. Sort: due_at, borrowed_at. Page size 25.
List the loans of one book.

workflows.name: loan_lifecycle
rules: Loans are created only by checkout_book. There is no generic create or update route for loans.

checkout_book takes book_id and member_id. Refused with 409 member_suspended if the member is suspended. Refused with 409 loan_limit if the member already has 5 open loans (active or overdue). Refused with 409 unpaid_fines if the member's unpaid fines are 1000 cents or more. Refused with 409 no_copies_available if the book's open loans already equal its copies. An unknown book or member is a 4xx input error.

A new loan is active. borrowed_at is the engine time, due_at is borrowed_at plus 21 days, renewals is 0, fine_cents is 0 and fine_paid is false. loan_ref is L plus a 5-digit sequence continuing after the CSV (L00301 first).
Unpaid fines for a member are the sum of fine_cents over their loans that are returned or overdue and have fine_paid false.

return_loan accepts an active or overdue loan. It sets returned_at to the engine time and the status to returned. The fine is 25 cents per full 24 hours past due_at, capped at 2000, and 0 if returned on time. Returning an already returned loan is 409 invalid_state.

renew_loan accepts only an active loan whose member is active. It adds 14 days to due_at and increments renewals. A third renewal is 409 renewal_limit. An overdue loan is 409 loan_overdue. A returned loan is 409 invalid_state. A suspended member is 409 member_suspended.

pay_fine accepts a returned loan with fine_cents > 0 and fine_paid false. It sets fine_paid true. Anything else is 409 no_fine_due. Fines on an overdue (unreturned) loan cannot be paid before the book is returned.
The accrue_overdue job moves active loans past due_at to overdue and keeps fine_cents at 25 cents per full day overdue (capped at 2000) for every overdue loan.

workflows.name: member_standing
rules: A new member is active. Staff move a member between active and suspended with a plain PATCH.
A suspended member cannot check out or renew, but can still return books and pay fines.

jobs.name: accrue_overdue
jobs.rule: For every active loan with due_at before now, set the status to overdue. For every overdue loan, set fine_cents to 25 times the number of full 24-hour periods past due_at, capped at 2000. Returned loans are never touched.

seed.mix: Books: all 200 CSV rows, with the 10 genres and 4 branches as in the file. Members: one per distinct member_id in the loans CSV (107), with generated plausible names and emails. About 10 are suspended and the rest active. Loans: all 300 CSV rows with isbn mapped to book_id and member_id to the member row. loan_ref is the CSV loan_id. Rows with returned_at set (about 77%) are returned. The unreturned rows (about 23%) are overdue if due_at is before clock.start and active otherwise, since due dates run to 2026-10-19. fine_cents comes from the CSV, and fine_paid is a mix of paid and unpaid on returned loans with a fine. Renewals are 0 to 2. The returned share may exceed 70%, because the CSV fixes it. A few anchor loans give the tasks one unambiguous target each.

assumptions.why: Every historical event in the CSV ends by 2026-09-30T21:00:00Z, so the world starts after them. 2026-10-07 is today's date. Some unreturned loans are due after the start (due dates run to 2026-10-19), so the seed holds both overdue and still-active unreturned loans. Time moves only through tests or the clock endpoint, which keeps tests exact.

assumptions.decision: Books use the CSV isbn as a unique string field, and loans reference the book by its row id (book_id). The seed maps loan.isbn to the book row.
assumptions.why: The ISBN is the natural key, but the engine's ref fields point at row ids. The 13-digit ISBN would lose any leading zeros as an int, so it is stored as a string.

assumptions.decision: The CSV copies column becomes book.copies. Availability is not stored. Checkout counts a book's open loans (active or overdue) against copies. If the seed already has more open loans than copies, availability is simply 0 and no seed row is changed.
assumptions.why: A stored availability counter could drift from the loans and complicates plain book create and update.

assumptions.decision: Members are not in the CSV. The seed creates one member per distinct loan member_id (107), with the CSV code kept in member.code, generated names and emails, and about 10 suspended.
assumptions.why: Loans need a member row to reference. A member state gives the suspension rule something to work on.

assumptions.decision: Loan period is 21 days, a renewal adds 14 days, there are at most 2 renewals, and the loan limit is 5 open loans.
assumptions.why: The CSV due_at is exactly 21 days after borrowed_at. The renewal figures are common library defaults.

assumptions.decision: Fine is 25 cents per full 24 hours overdue, capped at 2000 cents. Checkout is blocked at 1000 cents or more of unpaid fines. Fines are paid in full through pay_fine and only after the return.
assumptions.why: The CSV fine_cents values (e.g. 450 = 18 days) fit 25 cents a day. The cap and the block threshold are the simplest consistent policy, since the CSV carries no rules. Seed fines stay as given.

assumptions.decision: Loans are never created or edited through generic routes. Only checkout_book, return_loan, renew_loan and pay_fine write them, and the accrue_overdue job moves them to overdue. Book and member records have plain create, get, update and list routes. There is no delete route for books, members or loans.
assumptions.why: This forces agents to use the real circulation workflow, so rules such as fines and copy availability cannot be bypassed, and history is kept.

assumptions.decision: List routes use cursor mode with the default envelope (data, next_cursor). Searches use ?q=. The default error shape is {error:{code,message}}.
assumptions.why: These are the engine defaults, so agents see one consistent convention.

assumptions.decision: Acceptance tests use ISBNs 97900000000xx and member codes ACC-Mxx, which the CSV never uses. The ISBNs in the CSV start 9781.
assumptions.why: The tests create their rows through the API and must not collide with seed data. They run before any seed exists.

assumptions.decision: The routes checkout_book, return_loan, renew_loan and pay_fine in the route list share ids with workflow actions and are built as those actions, not as routes.
assumptions.why: The plan lists the public paths. The actions own the real behavior.

outOfScope.why: The CSV has no reservations. They need a queue and notifications beyond the loan lifecycle this world covers.

outOfScope.what: Staff accounts, authentication and branch permissions
outOfScope.why: Nothing in the CSV models them, and the tasks need only the public records API.

outOfScope.what: Real payments and refunds (card gateways, partial payments, fine waivers)
outOfScope.why: A fine is either paid in full or not. A payment system would be a separate world.

outOfScope.what: Inter-branch transfers and per-branch inventory counts
outOfScope.why: Each book belongs to one branch in the CSV. Moving copies adds a model the data does not support.

outOfScope.what: Email or SMS overdue notices, reports and dashboards
outOfScope.why: They are outputs, not state an agent changes.

outOfScope.what: Lost or damaged items and replacement charges
outOfScope.why: The CSV has no such state, and it would add a fourth loan state with its own money rules.

open_questions.question: Should members be separate records, given the CSV only has member_id strings on loans?
open_questions.default_answer: Yes. One member row per distinct loan member_id, with the CSV code kept in member.code and generated names.

open_questions.question: What are the loan period, renewal rules and loan limit?
open_questions.default_answer: 21 days, 14 days per renewal, at most 2 renewals, and 5 open loans per member.

open_questions.question: How are overdue fines calculated?
open_questions.default_answer: 25 cents per full 24 hours past due, capped at 2000 cents. Fines are charged when the book is returned and accrue on the loan while it is overdue.

open_questions.question: What happens when a member has unpaid fines?
open_questions.default_answer: At 1000 cents or more, checkout is refused until the fines are paid. Returns and fine payments always work.

open_questions.default_answer: Stored as a state (active, overdue, returned). A job moves active loans to overdue once due_at has passed.
